small_guidance:
- The kernel currently re-computes GELU twice (pass 1 stats + pass 2 normalize). Allocate a scratch buffer for `gx` (or keep it in registers across passes by tiling smaller) so the erf is computed once — this is pure compute waste on a memory-bound op.
- Try larger `BLOCK_SIZE` (4096) with `num_warps=8`, `num_stages=3` for the HW=65536 case; the per-(N,G) work is huge (8·65536 elems) so fewer outer iterations + better pipelining should help.
- Add `triton.autotune` over BLOCK_SIZE ∈ {1024, 2048, 4096} × num_warps ∈ {4, 8} × num_stages ∈ {2, 3} keyed on (HW, CPG).
large_guidance:
- The torch ConvTranspose2d dominates runtime here (output is 128×64×258×258 ≈ 2.2 GB tensor written then re-read). Replace it with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel (input × kernel outer-product scattered to output with stride/padding indexing) and fuse the GELU + GroupNorm tail directly — current design still pays the full conv-transpose cost plus an extra global write/read of the conv output.
- Alternative: since stride=1, kernel=3, ConvTranspose2d is equivalent to a padded direct Conv2d with flipped weights; implement as an im2col-style GEMM with the GELU fused into the epilogue, then a second kernel for GroupNorm over channels-last output. Channels-last layout makes the GN reduction stride-1 across HW.
- Fuse conv-transpose epilogue → GELU → partial reductions for GN stats in a single pass using atomics or a two-stage (per-tile partials, then per-group finalize) approach to avoid materializing the full conv output twice.
